answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, limiting influence to reachable paths rather than claimed identities. A sybil cluster, like a mesa of mutually endorsing nodes, may have many internal attestations yet connect outward through a sparse cut. Its low conductance restricts walk flow across that boundary and, with capped edge weights and a fixed honest seed distribution, bounds its aggregate voting weight; an oasis of internal agreement cannot turn a whisper into authority.
